why: A coffee machine needing 2 to 4 maintenance visits a year at $9 an hour of labour and using 1,000 to 1,200 kWh a year at 10c per kWh is believable.

Each country's Productivity and Hours shares add to exactly 100%, a share above 100% comes with negative Hours growth (a real decomposition result), and annual business sector growth of 1.4% to 4.8% is believable for European countries.
Revenue minus costs gives margins of 14.0% and 7.5% as stated, and a Paris family bakery selling about 19,000 to 20,000 items a month for about €38,000 (about €1.90 an item) is believable.
Translation and defect-fixing costs (55,000 and 17,000) sit within each line's total cost (60,000 and 25,000), and wages of $15 to $25 an hour and about $200 per fixed defect are believable.

584 to 1,147 cups a year per person (about 115 to 240 litres) is high but within a factor of a few of the heaviest real coffee-drinking countries, and cup costs of $0.40 to $0.80 under prices of $1.00 to $2.00 are believable.
The Area B Question 1 pie gives 12% + 12% + 57% + 41% + 18% = 140% of respondents, but a split of all respondents across five scores must add to 100%.
Market shares of 0.4% to 5.7% for a firm with a small emerging-market presence and pharmaceutical profit margins of 11% to 47% are believable, as is a $1.2 billion national prescription market.
An online department store with €450 to €585 million in revenue and category margins of 3% to 28% (high for fashion but within a few times the norm) is believable.
Zero deliveries on Saturday and Sunday match the weekday-only depot, and 8,800 tonnes a week against £9,600 of weekly staff cost is a very large, lean depot but not clearly a tenfold error.
Both pies add to 100%, the second is drawn from the 60% who came mainly for the Gallery, and 6,000 survey respondents in a month is believable for a city art gallery.
International plus domestic profit matches each year's total (20, 15, 15, 5), and the implied sales of £500 to £800 million at 1% to 2.5% margins are believable for a UK high-street baby retailer.

Revenues sit well below their markets (about 17% to 40% share), and revenue per representative of about $3 million (skin cancer) and $8 million (botulinum toxins) is high but within a factor of a few of what specialist pharma sales forces report.
Coffee shops serving 500 to 1,600 customers a day with 3 to 6 minute waits, a $1 million store and $2 profit per customer are believable.
Half a baker (80 hours) making 65 cakes a month and 2.5 bakers (400 hours) making 304 cakes, about 75 to 80 minutes of labour a cake, is slow but believable for a bakery making elaborate cakes.
Quintile 1 shows an average of -0.4 purchase transactions in the first 90 days, a negative count that also cannot coexist with its $79 of revenue from those transactions.
A $100 weekly fee, 0.2 tons of trash per customer a week, $15 a ton disposal and $2,000 a day for truck and crew give a break-even near 100 customers per truck, which is believable.
Each chain's cost shares and margin add to 100%, and 20,000 to 40,000 kg of shrimp per restaurant a year (about 55 to 110 kg a day) is believable for shrimp-focused restaurants.
Each stage of the mail flow is no larger than the one before it (100%, 70%, 70%, 61% and 100%, 65%, 63%, 52%), and about 1 billion items a month is believable for a national postal operator.
Regional coffee shop markets of $5 to $35 billion and emerging-market growth of about 20% a year are believable.
Table 1 gives December 38.0 days, but December has 31 days.
For large businesses, 3,565 currently use NGI, more than the 1,141 who currently use or have used it and more than the 2,865 surveyed in total.
A research publisher with $125 million in revenue across 12 products and 284 analysts (about $440,000 per analyst) is believable, even loss-making.
Regional offices raising £16 to £44 million a year on campaign costs of £1.1 to £4.4 million (7 to 23 pounds raised per pound spent) are high but within a factor of a few of real fundraising returns.

A chain of "about 100,000 seafood restaurants on the US Gulf Coast" is several times larger than the world's biggest restaurant chains and would mean only 12 El Diablo dishes per restaurant a year at 1.2 million dishes.

40 to 130 cars a week spending €10 each in the shop is low for a gas station but within a few times what a quiet station could report, and a 30% mini-market margin against the industry's 15% is a stated outperformance, not an impossibility.
Every country's project split adds to 100%, and PPP investment of $20 to $160 billion alongside GDP growth of 4% to 10% is believable for these emerging economies.
For a 40-store chain, 4,000 to 8,000 extra shoppers a day (100 to 200 per store), $8 to $10 gross profit per shopper and $12 to $40 million upgrades are believable.
